long.title: One Electron Interferes With Itself — in about a minute | Bear's Notes
long.description:
Fire electrons at two slits one at a time — each arrives as a single dot. Ten in, the dots look random; common sense says two heaps, one behind each slit. Seventy thousand in: stripes — bright and dark bands no two-heap picture allows.

A Brown Blue explainer, in the 3Blue1Brown tradition: concrete before abstract, mystery before formula.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
0:19 Waves vs particles
0:32 Interfering with itself

The single-electron double slit in about a minute: dots land one at a time, random at first — then 70,000 dots later, interference stripes. Each electron's wave goes through both slits and interferes with itself; the dot histogram is |ψ|²; and watching which slit kills the fringes. Full explainer (the buildup, de Broglie's λ = h/p, the forbidden bands) on the channel.

Source: Quantum Mechanics, Vol. 1, Ch. 2 — Matter Waves.
